newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai hotels' revenues up 17.9 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Dubai hotels' revenues up 17.9 pct in 1996.

text.p: Dubai's 233 hotels saw their revenues increase by 17.9 percent in 1996 to 1.7 billion dirhams ($463 million), the Department of Tourism and Commerce Marketing said.

"This was achieved on the back of a 4.5 percent increase of in the number of Dubai hotels...and an encouraging increase in visitors from some newer markets, such as the Far East and South Africa," the department's Enterprise Dubai publication said in its July issue.

It said visitors from Europe accounted for about 35.6 percent of the 1.8 million visitors to the Gulf emirate last year, making Europe the largest source of tourists to Dubai, one of the seven United Arab Emirates.
Dubai, the Gulf's trading hub, is implementing a five-year development plan aimed at diversifying its economy away from oil.
A study by Emirates Industrial Bank put the current contribution of tourism to Dubai's gross national product at 11 percent, but expected a 20 percent contribution by the year 2000.
